title: Non-Parametric Tests: Chi-Square and Associated Measures
summary: Chi-square (χ²) test; assumptions and conditions; non-parametric alternatives.
objectives: Define chi-square test and its purpose.
Calculate χ² and degrees of freedom.
revision: Chi-square for categorical data. χ² = Σ(O−E)²/E. Expected ≥ 5 per cell. df = (rows−1)(columns−1).

notes.t: A non-parametric test used to determine whether there is a significant association between categorical variables, or whether observed frequencies differ from expected frequencies.

i: Expected frequency in each cell should be adequate (commonly ≥ 5).

notes.t: χ² = Σ (O − E)² / E, where O = observed frequency and E = expected frequency. Degrees of freedom = (rows − 1) × (columns − 1) for a contingency table.

Worked example: Observed [30, 20], Expected [25, 25].
χ² = (30−25)²/25 + (20−25)²/25 = 25/25 + 25/25 = 1 + 1 = 2.0.
With df = 1, compare to critical value (3.84 at p < 0.05). 2.0 < 3.84 → not significant.
Chi-square is for categorical data. Expected frequency ≥ 5 per cell is a key condition. Frequently tested with contingency tables in UGC NET.
